functions.name: real_error
functions.description: Terminates the process on fatal error. Logs the event, closes john.pot and the log file, and exits with non-zero status. Typically not called directly; use the error(...) macro which fills file and line.
requirements: Must not return; callers should not expect control to continue after calling.
file should be a valid C string (usually __FILE__).
line should be the source line number (usually __LINE__).

functions.name: error
functions.description: Fatal error helper (macro) that logs the event, closes john.pot and the log file, and terminates the process with a non-zero exit status. This macro expands to real_error(__FILE__, __LINE__) and does not return. Use when encountering unrecoverable conditions where the program must abort immediately.
requirements: This call does not return; callers must not expect execution to continue after calling it.
Should only be used for fatal conditions where immediate termination is desired.
No arguments are required or used; any provided are ignored by the macro expansion.
Automatically annotates the call site with source file and line via __FILE__ and __LINE__.

functions.name: real_error_msg
functions.signature: void real_error_msg(const char *file, int line, const char *format, ...)
functions.description: Terminates the process on fatal error after printing a formatted error message. Then delegates to real_error to log and exit. Use the error_msg(...) macro to auto-fill file and line.
requirements: Uses printf-style formatting; format must be a valid format string for the provided variadic arguments.
Does not return; callers must not expect execution to continue.
file should be __FILE__ and line should be __LINE__ in normal use.

functions.name: error_msg
functions.description: Fatal error helper (macro) that prints a formatted error message and then terminates the process. Expands to real_error_msg(__FILE__, __LINE__, format, ...) which in turn calls real_error to perform final cleanup and exit. Intended for unrecoverable errors where an explanatory message should be shown. Does not return.
requirements: This call does not return; callers must not expect execution to continue after calling it.
format must be a valid printf-style format string; the variadic arguments must match the format specifiers.
Use for fatal conditions where you want to log a descriptive message before exiting.
Automatically annotates the call site with source file and line via __FILE__ and __LINE__.

functions.name: real_pexit
functions.signature: void real_pexit(const char *file, int line, const char *format, ...)
functions.description: Like perror() with formatting: prints a formatted message combined with the current errno text, then exits via error(). Use the pexit(...) macro to auto-fill file and line.
requirements: Uses printf-style formatting; format must match the provided variadic arguments.
Does not return; callers must not expect execution to continue.
file should be __FILE__ and line should be __LINE__ in normal use.

functions.name: pexit
functions.description: Formatted perror-like fatal error helper (macro). Similar to perror(), but supports printf-style formatting and then exits via error(). Expands to real_pexit(__FILE__, __LINE__, format, ...). Typically used immediately after a system/library call fails and errno is set, to include the OS error description along with a custom message. Does not return.
requirements: This call does not return; callers must not expect execution to continue after calling it.
format must be a valid printf-style format string; the variadic arguments must match the format specifiers.
Intended to be called in error paths where errno is meaningful (right after a failing call).
Automatically annotates the call site with source file and line via __FILE__ and __LINE__.

functions.name: write_loop
functions.signature: int write_loop(int fd, const char *buffer, int count)
functions.description: Attempts to write all count bytes from buffer to file descriptor fd, retrying as needed. Returns the number of bytes written, or -1 on error.
requirements: fd must be a valid open file descriptor supporting write.
buffer must point to at least count bytes of readable data.
count must be >= 0.
Caller must handle a return value of -1 as an error and partial writes otherwise.

functions.name: fgetl
functions.description: Reads a line from stream into s, stripping the trailing newline if present and skipping the remainder of overly long lines. Handles Unix and DOS newlines. Returns s on success or NULL on EOF/error.
requirements: s must point to a writable buffer of at least size bytes.
size should be > 0 to read any data.
stream must be a valid FILE* opened for reading.
Caller must check for NULL return to detect EOF/error.

functions.name: fgetll
functions.description: Reads a line from stream handling lines longer than size by allocating a larger buffer. Strips trailing newline. Returns a pointer to the line: either s (if it fit) or a newly allocated buffer; the latter must be freed by the caller via MEM_FREE.
requirements: s must point to a writable buffer of at least size bytes.
size should be > 0 for useful input.
stream must be a valid FILE* opened for reading.
If the returned pointer is not exactly s, the caller MUST free it with MEM_FREE when done.
Caller must check for NULL return to detect EOF/error.

functions.name: strncpy_pad
functions.signature: void *strncpy_pad(void *dst, const void *src, size_t size, uint8_t pad)
functions.description: Copies up to size bytes from src to dst like strncpy but pads any remaining bytes with the specified pad value instead of NUL. NUL-termination is not guaranteed.
requirements: dst must point to a writable buffer of at least size bytes.
src must point to a readable string or buffer of sufficient length.
size specifies the total number of bytes to write to dst.
Caller must not assume dst is NUL-terminated.

functions.name: strnfcpy
functions.description: Copies src to dst with a maximum of size bytes, writing at most one terminating NUL if there is room, and not padding the remainder (unlike strncpy).
requirements: dst must point to a writable buffer of at least size bytes.
size should be > 0 to allow writing a terminator.
src must be a valid C string.

functions.name: strnzcpy
functions.signature: inline char *strnzcpy(char *dst, const char *src, int size)
functions.description: Copies src to dst with a limit of size-1 characters and always NUL-terminates if size > 0. Returns dst.
requirements: dst must point to a writable buffer of at least size bytes.
src must be a valid C string.
If size < 1, the function writes nothing; caller should handle that case.

functions.name: strnzcpylwr
functions.description: Copies src to dst like strnzcpy but converts characters to lowercase during copy. Always NUL-terminates if size > 0. Returns dst.
requirements: dst must point to a writable buffer of at least size bytes.
src must be a valid C string.
Locale/encoding-specific behavior for case conversion is unspecified.

functions.name: strnzcpyn
functions.signature: inline int strnzcpyn(char *dst, const char *src, int size)
functions.description: Copies src to dst like strnzcpy and returns the resulting string length in dst. If size < 1, returns 0.
requirements: dst must point to a writable buffer of at least size bytes.
src must be a valid C string.
If size > 0, dst will be NUL-terminated.

functions.name: strnzcpylwrn
functions.signature: int strnzcpylwrn(char *dst, const char *src, int size)
functions.description: Copies src to dst with lowercase conversion like strnzcpylwr and returns the resulting length. Always NUL-terminates if size > 0.
requirements: dst must point to a writable buffer of at least size bytes.
src must be a valid C string.

functions.name: strnzcat
functions.description: Appends src to dst ensuring the total buffer size is respected and that dst is always NUL-terminated. Similar to strncat but safer by taking the total buffer size.
requirements: dst must point to a writable buffer of at least size bytes and contain a NUL-terminated string.
src must be a valid C string.
size must reflect the total capacity of dst, not the remaining space.

functions.name: strnzcatn
functions.signature: char *strnzcatn(char *dst, int size, const char *src, int max_src)
functions.description: Appends up to max_src characters from src to dst, protecting the dst buffer and always NUL-terminating. Safer concatenation with both total buffer size and max source length.
requirements: dst must point to a writable buffer of at least size bytes and contain a NUL-terminated string.
src must be a valid C string of at least max_src bytes if max_src is larger than the string length.
size must reflect the total capacity of dst.
max_src should be >= 0.

functions.name: atou
functions.description: Converts a decimal string to an unsigned int, correctly handling values exceeding INT_MAX (unlike atoi for unsigned data). Behavior on invalid input is unspecified.
requirements: src must be a NUL-terminated string representing a non-negative integer in base 10.
Caller should not pass negative signs or non-numeric text; handling is unspecified.

functions.name: strtokm
functions.description: Tokenizes string s1 using any of the delimiter characters in delimit, but unlike strtok, it returns empty tokens for adjacent, leading, or trailing delimiters. Case and reentrancy characteristics are unspecified.
requirements: s1 should be a mutable C string; the function will modify it by inserting NULs between tokens.
delimit must be a valid C string of delimiter characters.
Behavior for subsequent calls with s1 == NULL is unknown from this header; consult implementation if needed.

functions.name: jtr_itoa
functions.signature: const char *jtr_itoa(int num, char *result, int result_len, int base)
functions.description: Integer-to-string conversion for bases 2..36. Writes the textual representation of num into result, up to result_len bytes, and returns result. Always writes within the provided buffer; if too small, returns a truncated least-significant portion.
requirements: base must be between 2 and 36 inclusive.
result must point to a writable buffer of length at least result_len.
result_len should be >= 1; if < 1, the function returns a constant empty string (per comment).
Caller must tolerate truncation if result_len is too small.

functions.name: jtr_utoa
functions.signature: const char *jtr_utoa(unsigned int num, char *result, int result_len, int base)
functions.description: Unsigned integer-to-string conversion for bases 2..36. See jtr_itoa semantics; truncates if buffer too small.
requirements: base must be between 2 and 36 inclusive.
result must point to a writable buffer of length at least result_len.
result_len should be >= 1; if < 1, the function returns a constant empty string.
Caller must tolerate truncation if result_len is too small.

functions.name: jtr_lltoa
functions.signature: const char *jtr_lltoa(int64_t num, char *result, int result_len, int base)
functions.description: 64-bit signed integer-to-string conversion for bases 2..36. See jtr_itoa semantics; truncates if buffer too small.
requirements: base must be between 2 and 36 inclusive.
result must point to a writable buffer of length at least result_len.
result_len should be >= 1; if < 1, the function returns a constant empty string.
Caller must tolerate truncation if result_len is too small.

functions.name: jtr_ulltoa
functions.signature: const char *jtr_ulltoa(uint64_t num, char *result, int result_len, int base)
functions.description: 64-bit unsigned integer-to-string conversion for bases 2..36. See jtr_itoa semantics; truncates if buffer too small.
requirements: base must be between 2 and 36 inclusive.
result must point to a writable buffer of length at least result_len.
result_len should be >= 1; if < 1, the function returns a constant empty string.
Caller must tolerate truncation if result_len is too small.

functions.name: human_prefix
functions.description: Formats a potentially large integer using binary prefixes (Ki, Mi, Gi, etc.), e.g., 437281954 -> "417 Mi". Returns a pointer to an internal tiny allocation.
requirements: The returned pointer refers to memory allocated via mem_alloc_tiny that is not intended to be freed by the caller.
Each call "leaks" about 16 bytes; avoid calling in tight loops if memory is constrained.

functions.name: human_speed
functions.description: Formats a speed value into a human-readable string with a suffix like "c/s", potentially using prefixes, e.g., 437281954 -> "437281K c/s". Returns a pointer to an internal tiny allocation.
requirements: The returned pointer refers to memory allocated via mem_alloc_tiny that is not intended to be freed by the caller.
Each call "leaks" about 16 bytes; avoid calling in tight loops if memory is constrained.

functions.name: human_prefix_small
functions.description: Formats a small magnitude number using SI prefixes (n, u, m, etc.), e.g., 0.000123 -> "123 u". Returns a pointer to an internal tiny allocation.
requirements: The returned pointer refers to memory allocated via mem_alloc_tiny that is not intended to be freed by the caller.
Each call "leaks" about 16 bytes; avoid calling in tight loops if memory is constrained.

functions.name: lcm
functions.signature: unsigned int lcm(unsigned int x, unsigned int y)
functions.description: Computes the least common multiple of x and y (the smallest positive integer divisible by both).
requirements: x and y are treated as unsigned integers; behavior for zero values is not documented here.
Caller should handle potential overflow of the result for large inputs.

functions.name: ltrim
functions.description: Removes leading spaces from str in-place. Returns str (possibly advanced to first non-space depending on implementation).
requirements: str must be a mutable C string.
Only spaces are mentioned; handling of other whitespace is unspecified.

functions.name: rtrim
functions.description: Removes trailing spaces from str in-place. Returns str.
requirements: str must be a mutable C string.
Only spaces are mentioned; handling of other whitespace is unspecified.

functions.name: host_total_mem
functions.description: Returns the total physical memory of the host in bytes, or -1 if unknown.
requirements: Caller must handle a return value of -1 indicating the value is unavailable.

functions.name: host_avail_mem
functions.description: Returns the available physical memory of the host in bytes, or -1 if unknown. When running multiple forks or MPI processes on the same host, divide by the number of processes for per-process availability.
requirements: Caller must handle a return value of -1 indicating the value is unavailable.
If used for per-process planning in multi-process scenarios, caller should divide appropriately as noted.

functions.name: parse_bool
functions.description: Parses a string as a boolean, case-insensitively. Accepts y/yes/true/1/OPT_TRISTATE_NO_PARAM as true (1), n/no/false/0/OPT_TRISTATE_NEGATED as false (0). Returns -1 for anything else, including NULL.
requirements: string may be NULL; in that case the function returns -1.
Input matching is case-insensitive; exact handling of surrounding whitespace is unspecified.

functions.name: jtr_basename
functions.description: Portable basename() replacement. Returns a pointer to the last path component of name, with special handling for empty/NULL, drive letters, and both '/' and '\' separators. According to the comment, if name is NULL or empty, it returns "."; if name is only separators it returns a single separator. Intended as a safe alternative to basename().
requirements: name may be NULL; function will return "." in that case (per comment).
The returned pointer refers to an internal/static buffer or memory managed by the function (exact ownership is not documented). Avoid modifying or freeing it.
Handles DOS drive letters and both '/' and '\' separators; behavior for other encodings is unknown.

functions.name: jtr_basename_r
functions.description: Reentrant/thread-safe basename() replacement. Writes the last path component of name into buf with the same special handling described for jtr_basename. Intended for multithreaded use.
requirements: buf must be at least strlen(name) + 1 bytes, or PATH_BUFFER_SIZE + 1 as suggested in the comment.
buf must be writable and non-NULL.
name may be NULL; in that case, the function produces "." in buf (per comment).
Handles DOS drive letters and both '/' and '\' separators.

functions.name: strip_suffixes
functions.signature: char *strip_suffixes(const char *src, const char *suffixes[], int count);
functions.description: Removes known suffixes from the input string src. Likely iterates over suffixes[0..count-1] and strips matching ones. Returns a pointer to the resulting string (details on buffer ownership/aliasing are not documented).
requirements: src must point to a valid NUL-terminated string.
suffixes must point to an array of count pointers to NUL-terminated strings; count must be >= 0.
Ownership and lifetime of the returned string are not documented; do not assume it must be freed unless implementation confirms.

functions.name: memmem
functions.signature: void *memmem(const void *haystack, size_t haystack_len, const void *needle, size_t needle_len);
functions.description: Searches for the first occurrence of the byte sequence needle within haystack, examining exactly haystack_len and needle_len bytes. This is provided here as a fallback implementation on platforms lacking memmem; on others the system memmem may be used.
requirements: haystack points to at least haystack_len bytes (may be NULL only if haystack_len is 0; unspecified here).
needle points to at least needle_len bytes (may be NULL only if needle_len is 0; unspecified here).
Behavior for needle_len == 0 is not documented here (typical memmem returns haystack).

functions.name: sleep
functions.description: Portable sleep replacement on Windows toolchains without POSIX sleep. Suspends execution for approximately i seconds.
requirements: i is the number of seconds to sleep; must be a non-negative integer.
Return value semantics (remaining seconds on interruption vs. 0) are not documented here.

functions.name: strcasecmp
functions.description: Case-insensitive string comparison of two NUL-terminated strings. Provided via mappings or fallback implementation on platforms lacking strcasecmp.
requirements: dst and src must be pointers to NUL-terminated strings.
Return value is the usual strcmp-style tri-state integer; exact collation rules depend on locale/implementation (not specified here).

functions.name: strncasecmp
functions.signature: int strncasecmp(const char *dst, const char *src, size_t count);
functions.description: Case-insensitive comparison of up to count characters of two NUL-terminated strings. Provided via mappings or fallback implementation on platforms lacking strncasecmp.
requirements: dst and src must be pointers to NUL-terminated strings.
count limits the number of characters compared; any value is allowed.
Return value follows strcmp-style semantics.

functions.name: strlwr
functions.description: Converts a string to lowercase in-place. Defined or mapped depending on platform; provided here if not available.
requirements: s must be a writable, NUL-terminated string buffer.
The function modifies s in place and returns s.

functions.name: strupr
functions.description: Converts a string to uppercase in-place. Defined or mapped depending on platform; provided here if not available.
requirements: s must be a writable, NUL-terminated string buffer.
The function modifies s in place and returns s.

functions.name: jtr_atoll
functions.description: Fallback implementation of atoll (string to long long) for platforms lacking atoll/_atoi64.
requirements: Input must be a pointer to a NUL-terminated string; behavior for NULL is unspecified.
Parsing rules, base, and overflow behavior follow typical atoll semantics but are not documented here.

functions.name: memcpylwr
functions.signature: void memcpylwr(char *dst, const char *src, size_t n);
functions.description: Copies n bytes from src to dst, converting alphabetic characters to lowercase during the copy. Utility for case-normalized copies of fixed-length buffers.
requirements: dst must point to a writable buffer of at least n bytes.
src must point to a readable buffer of at least n bytes.
Buffers may overlap behavior is unspecified (treat as non-overlapping like memcpy).

functions.name: _fopen64
functions.description: 64-bit variant of fopen on certain platforms (Cygwin/MSVC) to open files with large-file support. Returns a FILE* stream on success or NULL on failure.
requirements: Fname must point to a valid path string.
type must be a valid mode string (e.g., "r", "rb", "w", etc.).
Caller is responsible for closing the returned FILE* with fclose().

functions.name: vc_fixed_snprintf
functions.signature: int vc_fixed_snprintf(char *Dest, size_t max_cnt, const char *Fmt, ...);
functions.description: MSVC-specific wrapper used as a POSIX-compliant snprintf replacement on MSVC versions prior to 2015. Writes formatted data to Dest up to max_cnt bytes including the terminating NUL.
requirements: Dest must point to a writable buffer of at least max_cnt bytes.
Fmt must be a valid format string for the provided arguments.
On truncation/encoding errors, exact return semantics mirror its implementation; not specified here.

functions.name: setenv
functions.signature: int setenv(const char *name, const char *val, int overwrite);
functions.description: Emulation of POSIX setenv using putenv on platforms lacking setenv (notably Windows toolchains). Sets or updates an environment variable.
requirements: name must be non-NULL and typically must not contain '=' (standard POSIX constraint; exact enforcement here is not documented).
val should be non-NULL; if NULL behavior is unspecified here.
overwrite controls whether an existing variable should be overwritten (0 to not overwrite, non-zero to overwrite), per usual POSIX semantics.

functions.name: strrev
functions.description: Reverses a NUL-terminated string in place. Provided where not available in the C library.
requirements: str must be a writable, NUL-terminated string.
Function modifies the buffer and returns str.

functions.name: strnlen
functions.description: Returns the length of the string s, but scans at most max bytes. If no NUL is found within max, returns max. Provided as a fallback where strnlen is missing.
requirements: s must point to at least max readable bytes unless it contains a NUL earlier.
Behavior for s == NULL is undefined.

functions.name: strcasestr
functions.description: Case-insensitive substring search. Returns a pointer to the first occurrence of needle in haystack, or NULL if not found. Provided for platforms (e.g., MinGW) lacking strcasestr.
requirements: haystack and needle must be valid NUL-terminated strings.
Return points into haystack; do not free or modify through it beyond what haystack allows.

functions.name: check_pkcs_pad
functions.signature: int check_pkcs_pad(const unsigned char *data, size_t len, int blocksize);
functions.description: Validates standard PKCS padding (e.g., PKCS#7) at the end of a buffer. On success, returns the net length (length without padding). On failure, returns -1.
requirements: data must point to a readable buffer of len bytes.
blocksize must be a positive integer; exact valid range is not documented here.
Padding validation expectations (e.g., len being a multiple of blocksize) are not fully documented; typical PKCS#7 requires the last block be padded.

functions.name: replace
functions.description: In-place character replacement/removal. Replaces every instance of character c in string with character n. If n is '\0', occurrences of c are removed and the rest of the string is compacted.
requirements: string must be a writable, NUL-terminated buffer.
Operation is in-place and may reduce the string length when n == '\0'.
Returns the input pointer string.

functions.name: valid_luhn
functions.description: Validates a string against the Luhn checksum. Returns non-zero if s is non-NULL, contains only digits, and ends with a correct Luhn check digit; returns 0 otherwise (including NULL or empty strings).
requirements: s may be NULL; the function will return false in that case.
s should be a NUL-terminated string containing only digits for a successful validation.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# We generate NUL-terminated C strings as bytes. The fuzz stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR()
# multiple times, so a single input buffer should contain several candidate strings
# plus a handful of numeric values. The harness typically slices the input stream
# to feed different calls. We'll therefore emit a sequence of TLV items to allow
# the fuzzer to pick diverse substrings:
#   [count][items...]
#   item := type(1B) | len(2B LE) | payload(len bytes) | NUL(1B)
# Types:
#   0x01: generic ASCII string
#   0x02: mixed-case alpha string (good for case-insensitive comps)
#   0x03: path-like string (for basename/setenv edge sanitizing)
#   0x04: numeric decimal string (for atou/jtr_atoll etc., if used elsewhere)
#   0x05: empty string (len==0, still includes trailing NUL)
# We also append a trailer with a few unsigned ints in LE for size/count parameters.
# The entire buffer remains <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ASCII_PRINT = ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(32, 127))


def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Include spaces, punctuation to exercise tokenizers
    alphabet = ASCII_PRINT
    s = ''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))
    return s.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')


def _rand_mixed_case(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters
    s = ''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))
    return s.encode('ascii')


def _rand_path(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Produce paths with both separators and optional drive letters
    parts: List[str] = []
    # Randomly choose style
    style = r.choice(['posix', 'win', 'mixed', 'root_only', 'only_seps'])
    if style == 'only_seps':
        seps = '/' if r.random() < 0.5 else '\\'
        return (seps * r.randint(1, 5)).encode('ascii')
    if style == 'root_only':
        return r.choice(['/','\\']).encode('ascii')
    if style in ('win', 'mixed') and r.random() < 0.7:
        drive = r.choice(string.ascii_letters) + ':'
        parts.append(drive)
    count = r.randint(0, 5)
    for _ in range(count):
        name_len = r.randint(0, 10)
        if name_len == 0:
            parts.append('')
        else:
            name_alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + '._- '
            parts.append(''.join(r.choice(name_alphabet) for _ in range(name_len)))
    # Random separators
    sep_choices = ['/', '\\'] if style != 'posix' else ['/']
    sep = r.choice(sep_choices)
    # Possibly start with separator (absolute)
    prefix = sep if r.random() < 0.5 else ''
    # Possibly duplicate separators to test case-insensitive search edge cases
    path = prefix + sep.join(parts)
    if style == 'mixed':
        # random replace some seps to mix
        path = ''.join((r.choice(sep_choices) if c in '/\\' and r.random()<0.5 else c) for c in path)
    # Maybe append trailing separator
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        path += r.choice(sep_choices)
    return path.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')


def _rand_numeric_str(r: random.Random, min_digits: int, max_digits: int) -> bytes:
    n = r.randint(min_digits, max_digits)
    if n == 0:
        return b''
    # Avoid leading zeros sometimes, include them sometimes
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        s = ''.join(r.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(n))
    else:
        first = r.choice(string.digits[1:])
        rest = ''.join(r.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(n-1))
        s = first + rest
    return s.encode('ascii')


def _pack_item(t: int, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    # length excludes trailing NUL; we ensure payload has no NUL inside for C-string semantics
    payload = payload.replace(b'\x00', b'?')
    ln = len(payload)
    return bytes([t & 0xFF]) + ln.to_bytes(2, 'little') + payload + b'\x00'


def _gen_strings(r: random.Random, target_budget: int) -> List[bytes]:
    items: List[bytes] = []
    # Seed with diverse corner cases helpful for case-insensitive ops
    fixed = [
        (0x02, b''),               # empty
        (0x02, b'a'),
        (0x02, b'A'),
        (0x02, b'ABC'),
        (0x02, b'abc'),
        (0x01, b''),               # empty generic
        (0x01, b'Hello, World!'),
        (0x01, b'\tleading and trailing spaces   '),
        (0x01, b'NUM=VALUE'),
        (0x03, b'/'),
        (0x03, b'\\'),
        (0x03, b'C:\\Path\\To\\File.txt'),
        (0x01, b'needle'),
        (0x01, b'NEEDLE'),
        (0x01, b'Haystack with a Needle inside'),
        (0x01, b'haystack with a needle inside'),
        (0x04, b'0'),
        (0x04, b'1'),
        (0x04, b'1234567890'),
    ]
    for t, p in fixed:
        items.append(_pack_item(t, p))
    # Randomly add more items
    extra = r.randint(10, 40)
    for _ in range(extra):
        t = r.choices([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], weights=[35, 30, 15, 15, 5], k=1)[0]
        if t == 1:
            p = _rand_ascii(r, 0, 80)
        elif t == 2:
            p = _rand_mixed_case(r, 0, 64)
        elif t == 3:
            p = _rand_path(r)
        elif t == 4:
            p = _rand_numeric_str(r, 0, 20)
        else:
            p = b''
        item = _pack_item(t, p)
        if sum(len(x) for x in items) + len(item) > target_budget:
            break
        items.append(item)
    return items


def _gen_uints_le(r: random.Random, count: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for _ in range(count):
        # Sizes up to ~2k, some zeros, some edge 0/1/1024
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.2:
            v = 0
        elif choice < 0.35:
            v = 1
        elif choice < 0.5:
            v = 1024
        else:
            v = r.randrange(0, 2048)
        out += int(v).to_bytes(4, 'little', signed=False)
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Reserve budget for trailer integers
    budget = MAX_TOTAL - 64
    items = _gen_strings(r, budget)
    count = len(items)
    header = b'JTR\x01' + count.to_bytes(2, 'little')
    body = b''.join(items)
    trailer_tag = b'\xAA\x55'  # simple marker
    trailer = trailer_tag + _gen_uints_le(r, 8)
    blob = header + body + trailer
    # Ensure size bound
    return blob[:MAX_TOTAL]

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator targets memmem fuzz stub, which pulls two FUZZ_PARAM_STR buffers.
# We return a single bytes blob that the harness will slice into two strings.
# Strategy: Construct a container encoding two lengths and two payloads.
# Layout:
#   [magic 4B] [hay_len 2B] [nee_len 2B] [flags 1B]
#   [hay_bytes hay_len] [nee_bytes nee_len]
# Where lengths are bounded to the stub caps (<=1024 and <=64). The flags control
# embedding relationships to exercise different behaviors:
#   bit0: ensure needle is a substring of haystack
#   bit1: ensure needle is NOT present in haystack
#   bit2: use repeated pattern needle (e.g., AAAA) and corresponding hay
#   bit3: include NULs inside both buffers
#   bit4: create multiple occurrences with needle at end
# The harness will treat them as opaque; FUZZ_PARAM_STR just reads bytes. We thus
# self-describe so the consumer can feed consistent buffers.

MAGIC = b"MMEM"
MAX_HAY = 1024
MAX_NEE = 64

def _rand_bytes(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Bias towards ASCII, but include full range
    out = bytearray()
    for _ in range(n):
        t = r.randrange(100)
        if t < 60:
            out.append(r.randrange(32, 127))  # printable
        elif t < 80:
            out.append(r.randrange(0, 32))    # control bytes including NUL possible later via flag
        else:
            out.append(r.randrange(0, 256))   # any
        
    return bytes(out)

def _with_nuls(r: random.Random, b: bytes, ratio: float = 0.1) -> bytes:
    if not b:
        return b
    ba = bytearray(b)
    count = max(1, int(len(ba) * ratio))
    for _ in range(count):
        idx = r.randrange(len(ba))
        ba[idx] = 0
    return bytes(ba)

def _mk_repeated_pattern(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Create a short alphabet pattern then repeat
    alphabet_choices = [b"A", b"AB", b"ABC", b"01", b"xyz", b"\x00\xff"]
    base = r.choice(alphabet_choices)
    reps = max(1, min(max_len // max(1, len(base)), r.randint(1, max(1, max_len // max(1, len(base))))))
    data = (base * reps)[:max_len]
    return data

def _embed(hay: bytes, needle: bytes, r: random.Random, ensure_present: bool, multi_occ: bool) -> (bytes, bytes):
    if not needle:
        return hay, needle
    if ensure_present:
        # Place needle at random positions; if multi_occ, place multiple times and end-aligned
        hay_len = len(hay)
        nee_len = len(needle)
        if hay_len < nee_len + 1:
            hay = hay + _rand_bytes(r, nee_len + 1)
            hay_len = len(hay)
        ba = bytearray(hay)
        positions: List[int] = []
        if multi_occ:
            # put at start, middle, and end if room
            positions = [0]
            mid = max(0, (hay_len - nee_len) // 2)
            positions.append(mid)
            positions.append(max(0, hay_len - nee_len))
        else:
            positions = [r.randrange(0, max(1, hay_len - nee_len + 1))]
        for pos in positions:
            end = pos + nee_len
            if end > len(ba):
                continue
            ba[pos:end] = needle
        hay = bytes(ba)
        return hay, needle
    else:
        # Try to avoid accidental inclusion by filtering occurrences
        if not hay or not needle:
            return hay, needle
        # If needle occurs, flip random hay bytes to avoid match
        while True:
            idx = hay.find(needle)
            if idx == -1:
                break
            ba = bytearray(hay)
            flip_pos = idx + r.randrange(len(needle))
            ba[flip_pos] ^= 0xFF
            hay = bytes(ba)
        return hay, needle

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose lengths with bias to interesting edges
    hay_len_choices = [0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, 64, 65, 127, 255, 256, 512, 1023, 1024]
    nee_len_choices = [0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 15, 31, 32, 33, 63, 64]
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        hay_len = r.choice(hay_len_choices)
    else:
        hay_len = r.randint(0, MAX_HAY)
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        nee_len = r.choice(nee_len_choices)
    else:
        nee_len = r.randint(0, MAX_NEE)

    hay_len = min(MAX_HAY, hay_len)
    nee_len = min(MAX_NEE, nee_len)

    flags = 0
    # Decide scenario
    scenario = r.randrange(6)
    # 0: ensure present
    # 1: ensure not present
    # 2: repeated pattern
    # 3: include nuls
    # 4: multi occurrences with end aligned
    # 5: random

    if scenario == 0:
        flags |= 0b00001
    elif scenario == 1:
        flags |= 0b00010
    elif scenario == 2:
        flags |= 0b00100
    elif scenario == 3:
        flags |= 0b01000
    elif scenario == 4:
        flags |= 0b10001  # ensure present + multi-occ at end
    else:
        pass

    # Generate base buffers
    if flags & 0b00100:
        needle = _mk_repeated_pattern(r, nee_len)
        hay = _mk_repeated_pattern(r, hay_len)
    else:
        needle = _rand_bytes(r, nee_len)
        hay = _rand_bytes(r, hay_len)

    # Optionally add NULs
    if flags & 0b01000:
        hay = _with_nuls(r, hay, ratio=0.2)
        needle = _with_nuls(r, needle, ratio=0.3)

    # Handle embedding constraints
    ensure_present = bool(flags & 0b00001)
    multi_occ = bool(flags & 0b10000)
    hay, needle = _embed(hay, needle, r, ensure_present, multi_occ)

    # Edge consistency: if needle longer than hay and ensure_present, extend hay
    if ensure_present and len(needle) > 0 and len(hay) < len(needle):
        hay += _rand_bytes(r, len(needle) - len(hay))

    # Build container
    # Ensure total size <= 4096
    header = MAGIC + struct.pack('>H', len(hay)) + struct.pack('>H', len(needle)) + bytes([flags & 0xFF])
    total = len(header) + len(hay) + len(needle)
    if total > 4096:
        # Trim hay to fit
        max_hay = max(0, 4096 - (len(header) + len(needle)))
        hay = hay[:max_hay]
        header = MAGIC + struct.pack('>H', len(hay)) + struct.pack('>H', len(needle)) + bytes([flags & 0xFF])

    return header + hay + needle

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: environment variable name
# We need to generate interesting valid strings for FUZZ_PARAM_STR used as
# - name: must be non-empty, should not contain '=', typically [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*
# - value: any string is fine (including empty), typical env var values
# The fuzzer stub truncates: name up to 32 bytes, value up to 128 bytes, and replaces '=' in name.
# We will produce a single buffer that the harness will split into two FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls in order.
# Convention for our generator: emit two NUL-terminated strings concatenated: name\0value
# This lets typical fuzz harnesses or custom adaptors pick them up. If not, it's still safe bytes.
# Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

SAFE_FIRST_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + "_"
SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"

COMMON_NAMES: List[str] = [
    "PATH", "HOME", "USER", "SHELL", "TMPDIR", "LANG", "TERM", "PWD", "OLDPWD",
    "EDITOR", "VISUAL", "LOGNAME", "HOSTNAME", "DISPLAY", "TZ", "LC_ALL",
    "_", "A", "Z", "VAR", "__very_long_env_var_name__", "LD_PRELOAD", "LD_LIBRARY_PATH"
]

COMMON_VALUES: List[str] = [
    "", "0", "1", "true", "false", "yes", "no", "/tmp", "/usr/bin:/bin", ".:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin",
    "en_US.UTF-8", "C", "UTF-8", "C.UTF-8", "~/.cache", "special_chars_!@#$%^&*()[]{}",
    "a" * 127,  # near truncation boundary for value (128)
    "x" * 200,  # will be truncated by stub
]


def _rand_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix of common and random safe names; ensure no '=' and non-empty
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.4:
        name = rng.choice(COMMON_NAMES)
    else:
        max_len = rng.randint(1, 32)  # stub will cap to 32
        first = rng.choice(SAFE_FIRST_CHARS)
        rest_len = max_len - 1
        rest = "".join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(rest_len))
        name = first + rest
    # Occasionally add digits or underscores near the end to vary
    if rng.random() < 0.2 and len(name) < 32:
        name += rng.choice(["_", str(rng.randint(0, 9))])
    # Ensure valid and no '='
    name = name.replace("=", "_")
    if not name:
        name = "VAR"
    return name


def _rand_value(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Values can be arbitrary bytes, but we’ll keep to printable with some edge cases
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.5:
        val = rng.choice(COMMON_VALUES)
    else:
        # Generate random length up to 256 (stub caps at 128)
        length = rng.randint(0, 256)
        # Include a wide range of characters including spaces and punctuation
        alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "
        val = "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))
        # Occasionally include path-like or key=value payloads (the name '=' will be sanitized anyway)
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            parts = [
                "/tmp", "/var/tmp", "/usr/local/bin", ".", "~",
                "C:\\Windows\\System32", "C:\\Temp",
            ]
            val = rng.choice(parts) + (":" + rng.choice(parts) if rng.random() < 0.5 else "")
    # Sometimes include newline or embedded NUL-like terminators? Can't embed NUL in Python str; keep printable.
    # The fuzz stub uses c_str(), so NUL would terminate early; we avoid actual NULs here.
    return val


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Create sets of candidates to encourage diversity per seed
    names = []
    values = []

    # Generate 1 primary pair, plus optional alternates packed together; but the stub will only use first two FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
    # We therefore emit just one name and one value separated by a NUL, and terminate with another NUL for safety.
    name = _rand_name(rng)
    value = _rand_value(rng)

    # Ensure lengths will be meaningful with stub caps
    if len(name) < 3 and rng.random() < 0.5:
        name = (name + "__")[:32]
    if len(value) == 0 and rng.random() < 0.5:
        value = "0"

    # Build buffer: name\0value\0
    # Keep total under 4096
    encoded_name = name.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')[:32]
    encoded_value = value.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')[:2048]

    buf = bytearray()
    buf += encoded_name + b"\x00" + encoded_value + b"\x00"

    # Add some additional trailing noise that could be used by other consumers, but keep valid core first.
    if len(buf) < 1024 and rng.random() < 0.3:
        extra = _rand_value(rng).encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')[:256]
        buf += extra

    return bytes(buf[:4096])
